headline: Gold hits a 52 week low and Nasdaq drops 2.9 percent as Intel and Amazon deepen AI fears
subhead: Gold fell 3.6 percent to 3,885 dollars and silver 5.9 percent, the S&P 500 lost 1.8 percent, and Bitcoin held near 77,200 dollars after the Binance hack.

us.text: The S&P 500 fell 1.8 percent to 7,580 and the Nasdaq 2.9 percent to 25,437 as Intel and Amazon results revived AI spending worries.
Amazon reported trailing free cash flow of minus 42.4 billion dollars on AI capex and kept 2026 spending near 220 billion.
Next week turns on Apple results on 2 November, the US midterm elections on 3 November and October payrolls on 6 November.

india.text: Nifty 50 closed at 23,053.10 and the Sensex rose 308 points to 74,459.53 on 30 October, led by IT and pharma.
FIIs were net buyers of 3,598.54 crore rupees in cash on 30 October while DIIs sold a net 817.51 crore (provisional).
The rupee gained 33 paise to close at 94.93 per dollar on a weaker dollar and firmer local stocks.

global.text: Asia was mixed on AI worries: Japan and South Korea fell with chipmakers while Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained; the Bank of Japan held rates.
The STOXX 600 slipped to about 646.75 and the DAX to about 25,818 as Intel's guidance hit European chip names.
Gold fell 3.6 percent to a 52 week low below 3,900 dollars as a Hormuz tanker attack lifted oil and Fed hike fears.

weekly.narrative: The week turned on whether AI spending pays: Alphabet had its worst day on record after negative free cash flow, ServiceNow and Caterpillar sank on guidance, and Intel and Amazon closed the week with a broad tech sell-off that left the Nasdaq down 2.0 percent and the S&P 500 down 0.6 percent. The Fed held rates on 28 October with two officials favouring a hike, and with oil lifted by fresh Hormuz attacks, rate fears hit metals hardest: gold lost 3.1 percent on the week to a 52 week low and silver 8.5 percent. India moved the other way, with the Nifty back above 23,000 on IT and pharma buying, Trent jumping on results and foreign investors turning net buyers on Friday. Crypto absorbed a 6.3 billion dollar Binance hack, leaving Bitcoin down 4.4 percent for the week near 77,200 dollars. Next week brings Apple results on 2 November, the US midterm elections on 3 November, the Bank of England on 5 November and US payrolls on 6 November.
